description: A chaotic CV source: a Henon or Ikeda attractor stepped forward at a rate you set or at an external clock, with its two coordinates on the outputs and a gate for every step

params.text: Sets how often a new value is taken, on a logarithmic scale from one every 20 seconds fully left to 500 a second fully right; it is ignored while CLOCK is patched
Adds -2V to +2V to both CV outputs
Sets how much of each step the gate output stays high, from a thousandth of it to all of it
Chooses which attractor is stepped: Henon or Ikeda
Sets the constant the attractor is built on, mapped to between 0.7 and 1.0, which changes the run of values it produces

inputs.text: Takes the tempo from the time between two rising edges past 2V, one new value to the beat, and takes over from RATE

outputs.text: 10V for the fraction of each step set by GATE and 0V for the rest of it
The attractor's first coordinate with BIAS added, held at that value until the next step
The attractor's second coordinate with BIAS added, held at that value until the next step

notes: in Ikeda mode the step rate also follows the attractor's own magnitude, so the steps come unevenly; in Henon mode that term is one and the rate is steady
the attractor is put back to its starting point whenever a coordinate reaches -2.2V in Henon mode or -2V in Ikeda mode, which is what stops it sticking
all three outputs are one channel, and the two CV outputs hold their value between steps

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the RATE knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
